answer: A tail-value-at-risk filter prices each agent’s stake against a modeled ripple of correlated identity losses, so a sybil cluster must post collateral covering the 99.5th-percentile joint shortfall rather than the mean. Entry then requires a lotus of cross-validated attestations whose dependence structure is estimated like hurricane co-occurrence, forcing attackers to pay for genuinely uncorrelated credentials. A spiral of escalating premiums follows repeated near-miss clusters, but the limit is model risk: a novel correlation regime underprices the first attack.
